tasks.title: Publish the graph's skip count in expand's coverage totals and word its summary from coverage.skipped

details.goal: Make `expand`'s `what: "coverage"` answer publish the repo-wide skipped-path count in `totals.not_indexed_total` — the same number `status` and `summary` publish for one generation — while its summary sentence keeps printing the requested prefix's own count, read from `coverage.skipped`. No new key, no new query, no change to any other `expand` answer.
steps: Add `notIndexedTotal: number` to `Scoped` with its doc comment.
Return `notIndexedTotal: assembly.notIndexedTotal` from `scopeOf`.
Give `coverageSummary` a `skipped: number` parameter, delete its `totals.not_indexed_total ?? payload.not_indexed.length` line, and comment why the number is the scope's.
In `coverageAnswer`, publish `not_indexed_total: scope.notIndexedTotal` and pass `scope.coverage.skipped` / `env.coverage.skipped` to both `coverageSummary` calls.
Run the scoped checks below and quote the numbers.

tasks.title: Re-point expand's folder-coverage fixture at divergent counts and add the cross-tool agreement case

details.goal: Prove the issue's two acceptance criteria against one fixture generation: `status`, `summary` and `expand` publish an identical `totals.not_indexed_total` when skipped rows exist outside the requested prefix, and `expand`'s own scope count is still readable as `coverage.skipped`. Also re-point the existing folder-coverage assertion at a fixture where the graph count and the prefix count differ, so the case can actually fail.
details.contract:
One file: `tests/tools-expand.test.ts` — doc comment `:34-45`, the `skipped` fixture row `:153-159`, the `rowsForPaths` stub `:288-297`, `notIndexedAll` / `notIndexedCount` at `:301-302`, the folder-coverage assertion at `:616`. It is hermetic already (a hand-written `GraphReader`, `mkdtemp` temp roots removed in `afterAll`); keep it that way — no database, no network, no writes inside the repository.

(1) Fixture. Next to the existing `skipped` row (`:153-159`) add six literal rows and point the reader's two members at them:
```ts
/** Six skipped paths no requested prefix covers, plus the folder's own: this fixture's graph
 * count (7) deliberately exceeds what `rowsForPaths` can reach (1), because a fixture whose two
 * counts coincide cannot tell the repo-wide total from the scope's count. */
const OUTSIDE_SKIPS: readonly SkippedPathRow[] = [
  { id: 30, path: "docs/legacy.xslt", reason: "grammar_unavailable", detail: null, language: null },
  { id: 31, path: "docs/notes.markdown", reason: "grammar_unavailable", detail: null, language: null },
  { id: 32, path: "scripts/build.sh", reason: "unsupported_ext", detail: null, language: null },
  { id: 33, path: "vendor/min.js", reason: "size_cap", detail: null, language: null },
  { id: 34, path: "assets/logo.svg", reason: "unsupported_ext", detail: null, language: null },
  { id: 35, path: "config/settings.yaml", reason: "unsupported_ext", detail: null, language: null },
];
```
Six rows, distinct ids (`30`-`35`) and paths, none under `FOLDER_PREFIX` (`src/widgets`) and none under `A_PATH` (`src/a.ts`). Reader members become `notIndexedAll: () => [...OUTSIDE_SKIPS, skipped],` and `notIndexedCount: () => OUTSIDE_SKIPS.length + 1` (= 7). Leave `rowsForPaths` (`:288-297`) unchanged: it is keyed by prefix and returns the first match, which is why the reachable scope count stays 1 while the graph count is 7.

(2) `:616` (`a folder target infers coverage of the prefix, both halves included`): `expect(env.totals.not_indexed_total).toBe(1)` becomes `expect(env.totals.not_indexed_total).toBe(OUTSIDE_SKIPS.length + 1)`, and the same test gains `expect(env.coverage.skipped).toBe(1)` and `expect(env.summary).toContain("1 not indexed")`. Do not merely flip the expected value without the fixture change: the two counts must differ in the fixture, not only in the assertion.

(3) New `describe("expand: the graph's skip total versus the scope's count")`, placed after `expand: inference`, with a `beforeAll` that sets `repoRoot = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "sangkar-expand-total-"))`, pushes it to `dirs`, `mkdirSync(join(repoRoot, "src", "widgets"), { recursive: true })`, writes `src/a.ts` and `src/widgets/x.ts` with one trivial function each, then `ctx = makeContext(makeFixture().reader, repoRoot)`. Imports to add at the top: `import { handle as statusHandle } from "../src/tools/status/handler";` and `import { handle as summaryHandle } from "../src/tools/summary/handler";` (aliased, because `handle` is already `expand`'s).
One test, `test("status, summary and expand agree on totals.not_indexed_total for one generation", async () => { ... })`, makes exactly three calls on that one `ctx`:
- `const expanded = await handle(ctx, { target: FOLDER_PREFIX });` (a folder infers `what: "coverage"`)
- `const statusEnv = statusHandle(ctx, { paths: [FOLDER_PREFIX] });` (synchronous)
- `const summaryEnv = await summaryHandle(ctx, { scope: "area", target: FOLDER_PREFIX });`
and asserts, with `const expectedTotal = OUTSIDE_SKIPS.length + 1;`:
```ts
const published = [expanded.totals.not_indexed_total, statusEnv.totals.not_indexed_total, summaryEnv.totals.not_indexed_total];
expect(published).toEqual([expectedTotal, expectedTotal, expectedTotal]);
expect(expanded.coverage.skipped).toBe(1);
expect(coverageOf(expanded).not_indexed.length).toBe(1);
expect(expanded.summary).toContain("1 not indexed");
expect(expanded.summary).not.toContain(`${expectedTotal} not indexed`);
expect(statusEnv.coverage.skipped).toBe(1);
```
Guard `expanded.status === "ok"` before the payload access, and use `coverageOf(expanded)` for it. The negative assertion is computed, never a literal 7: it must break if the fixture's row count changes without the case being re-thought. `summary`'s `scope: "area"` keeps the case off the change-set path; a `summary.change.degraded` warning on the temp non-git root is expected and is not an error.

(4) Extend the file's top doc comment (`:34-45`) by one sentence: the same fake reader also pins that all three tools publish the graph's skip total while each prints its own scope's count. Do not touch `tests/tools-summary.test.ts` (`:730-757` already pins the summary side) and do not weaken any existing assertion.
steps: Add the six-row `OUTSIDE_SKIPS` list beside the existing `skipped` row and point `notIndexedAll` / `notIndexedCount` at it.
Re-point the `:616` folder-coverage assertion at the graph's count and add its `coverage.skipped` and summary-sentence assertions.
Add the aliased `statusHandle` and `summaryHandle` imports.
Add the new `describe` with its own temp root and the one cross-tool test, with the computed negative assertion.
Add the one-sentence doc-comment note and run the checks below.

(1) §1.1 key table, `:97` — the `totals.not_indexed_total` row. Today it ends "… `status` and `summary` report the same number for one generation, so a narrow scope cannot understate what the repository never read". Change the tool list so it names all three: `status`, `summary` and `expand` report the same number for one generation. Keep the rest of the row's meaning (repo-wide, read from the graph, never from this answer's list). Do not touch the `coverage.skipped` row at `:95` — it already lists `expand` among the tools where `skipped` is `not_indexed.length`, which stays true — nor the `coverage.tests` row.

(2) §7, `:794-797` — the paragraph beginning "A `what: "coverage"` answer is scoped to the prefix it was asked about". (3) Re-read §7's example envelopes and report the finding. At `dc5a548` the check is `sed -n '800,916p' docs/my-product/TOOLS-SPEC.md | grep -n not_indexed_total` → 0 matches.
